name: Genista Cottage
address: Genista Cottage, Drishoge, Ballyboughal, Co. Dublin
agent: Gráinne McKenna, DNG McKenna Healy, Skerries
questions: Genista Cottage is on Fingal's Record of Protected Structures (RPS 0152). Both bedrooms and the only shower room are upstairs, and Gabor's parents need to sleep on the ground floor. Has anyone looked at a single-storey bedroom and shower-room extension, or at converting the 2.88 × 4.57 m studio? Has there been any pre-planning or conservation-officer advice on either?
Are the studio and the garden room insulated, wired and heated? Are either plumbed, or close to a drain? Were they built as exempt development or with permission?

When was the cottage last rethatched or re-ridged, in what material, and by whom? Is there a thatcher's condition report? Who insures it now, at what premium, and on what fire conditions (stove, chimneys, spark arrestors, alarms)? Have any heritage thatching grants been drawn down?

Is water mains or a private well? Is foul drainage a septic tank or a treatment plant, and when was it last desludged? What fuel is the central heating? The BER shows 'pending'. Will there be a BER, or is the cottage exempt as a protected structure?

Can you send the folio map? From the drone shot the site is L-shaped and wraps around the neighbouring bungalow. What does 'potential for further development' mean in practice: an extension, or a site? Where is the secondary rear access, and is the whole boundary secure for two dogs?

ai.why: A protected 19th-century thatched cottage in walk-in condition, on 0.69 ac of lovely gardens with two garden rooms, about 15 minutes from Dublin Airport. It has real charm, but at about 69 m² it is far too small for six: two bedrooms, one shower room, nothing to sleep in on the ground floor, and €590k with thatch upkeep on top.

electricity.detail: Likely connected. Not stated, but the house is lived in and the garden studio has lights and sockets.

water.detail: Not stated in the listing. It is a rural lane, so the supply could be mains or a well. Ask.

sewer.detail: Not stated. On a rural site this is probably a septic tank or treatment plant. Ask for its age and service history.

internet.detail: Full fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband — 100 Mb full fibre'). The listing doesn't mention broadband, and the provider isn't confirmed.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: None in the cottage. Bedroom 1 (3.56 × 4.17 m), Bedroom 2 (2.56 × 1.88 m) and the only shower room are all upstairs, reached by a stair from the living room. The ground floor has just the living room, the kitchen and a utility room, so converting a room there would cost the family its only sitting room. The realistic route is the 2.88 × 4.57 m (13 m²) garden studio, which the photos show already set up with a bunk bed, sofa and stove. It would fit a double, but it has no WC or shower and sits across the garden. Because the cottage is a protected structure (RPS 0152), making it habitable, or extending the cottage, would need planning.

bedsNote: Bedroom 1 is a double (3.56 × 4.17 m, with a fireplace). Bedroom 2 is a box room (2.56 × 1.88 m). Both are upstairs, with a 2.45 × 1.60 m shower room. In the garden there is a 2.88 × 4.57 m studio, furnished with a bunk bed in the photos, and a 2.79 × 3.72 m garden room.
heating: Not stated. Photos show radiators and a multi-fuel stove in the living room; the fuel for the central heating is unknown.
tagline: A late-19th-century two-storey thatched cottage of about 69 m², on Fingal's Record of Protected Structures, with 0.69 ac of landscaped gardens, two garden rooms and a greenhouse. It is on Drishoge Lane between Ballyboughal and Oldtown, about 15 minutes from Dublin Airport.

pros.text: Genuine charm: a period thatched cottage in walk-in condition
pros.detail: Fingal's RPS 0152 describes it as a 'late 19th century two-storey thatched dwelling with bonneted gable'. It has lime-white walls, green joinery, pine floors and a multi-fuel stove, and it is described as lovingly maintained.

pros.text: 0.69 ac of mature, private gardens for the dogs and boys
pros.detail: About 0.28 ha: cottage-garden planting, a 'secret garden', a long striped lawn, a patio, a pergola with a barbecue, a greenhouse and a concrete pad. Hedges and trees line most of the boundary.

pros.text: Two garden rooms: home office plus a guest room
pros.detail: A 2.88 × 4.57 m timber studio with French doors, furnished in the photos with a bunk bed, sofa and stove, and a 2.79 × 3.72 m garden room. That is about 23.5 m² outside the house.

pros.text: Close to Dublin and the airport
pros.detail: Roughly 10 km (about 15 min) to Swords, 13 km (about 15–20 min) to Dublin Airport, and 30 min to the city by car via the M1 or M50 (BuyerIQ: 'Dublin within 30 min by car'). These are estimates; the trip cards give live times.

Per the listing it has a Mace shop, a pharmacy, a co-ed national school (about 210–236 pupils), a church, a GAA club, and pitch and putt. Oldtown, about 2.5 km the other way, has another national school.
CHI Temple Street is about 25 km by the M1, about 25–30 min at night. Our Lady of Lourdes in Drogheda (all ages) is about 30 km up the M1.
BuyerIQ shows 100 Mb full fibre for this Eircode, which is enough for home working from the garden studio.

cons.text: Far too small for six: about 69 m², two bedrooms, one shower room
cons.detail: The floor-plan rooms sum to about 69 m² (39 m² downstairs, 30 m² up), against a 100 m² minimum. Bedroom 2 is a 2.56 × 1.88 m box room. The only living space is an 18 m² living room plus a 3.56 × 2.85 m kitchen-dining room. That works out at €8,550 per m².
Both bedrooms and the 2.45 × 1.60 m shower room are up a narrow timber stair from the living room. The parents' room would have to be the 13 m² garden studio (no WC or shower) or a new extension.

cons.text: Protected structure (Fingal RPS 0152): changes are tightly controlled
cons.detail: Any extension, a ground-floor bedroom wing, window changes and the thatch itself need conservation-led planning and like-for-like materials. The listing's 'development potential' is subject to that, and to Fingal's rural housing policy.

ROUGH, unquoted: a full rethatch of a two-storey cottage roof (about 130–170 m² of thatch) runs roughly €30–50k every 20–35 years, with ridge renewal every 10–15 years at about €5–10k, so set aside about €2–3k a year. Insurance is likely €1,500–3,500 a year (owners report about 1.5–4× standard cover) from very few insurers. Heritage thatch grants (BHIS) can offset part of the cost.
Within the up-to-€700k allowance for charm near Dublin, but about €90k over the usual budget before any extension. Stamp duty is about €5,900.

cons.text: No station within reach on foot
cons.detail: Rush & Lusk is about 13 km away (about 17 min by car, then about 28–33 min to Connolly). Donabate is about 16 km (about 20 min, then about 23–28 min). Malahide is about 17 km (about 25 min, then about 18–30 min). Skerries is about 19 km (about 24 min, then about 35–44 min). Drive times are estimates.

cons.text: Neighbour's bungalow close by, cottage gable on the lane
cons.detail: The drone shots show the site wrapping around a neighbouring bungalow about 25–35 m from the cottage, and the cottage's gable sits a few metres from Drishoge Lane, a quiet country lane.
Water, drainage and heating fuel aren't stated, and the BER is 'pending'. BuyerIQ flags a moderate radon area (remediation about €800–2,000 if needed).
